words.gloss: those who have the nature of

parts.gloss: I will not (negative first-person singular suffix)

literal: Women of feminine nature all with eyes in common will consume; I will not approach, O playboy, your chest.
translation: All women feast upon your chest with their eyes as if it were common property; therefore, O playboy, I will not embrace your chest.
modern: பெண் தன்மை உடையவர்கள் எல்லாரும் உன்னுடைய மார்பைத் தங்கள் கண்களால் பொதுவானதாக நுகர்கிறார்கள்; பரத்தனே, அதனால் நான் உன்னுடைய மார்பைத் தழுவ மாட்டேன்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine expresses her feigned anger towards her lover by calling him a playboy ('paratta'). She accuses him of being so attractive that all women feast upon his chest with their eyes, making his chest a 'common property' shared by everyone. Because his chest is thus 'consumed' by the gaze of other women, she proudly refuses to touch or embrace it, claiming she does not want something that is shared publicly. This playful jealousy highlights the intimacy and the subtle, teasing conflicts between lovers.
